label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I ii q.94…: A proposition is self-evident in itself when its…
locator: I-II q.94 a.2 co.: Secundum se quidem quaelibet propositio dicitur per se nota, cuius praedicatum est de ratione subiecti; contingit tamen quod ignoranti definitionem subiecti, talis propositio non erit per se nota
interpretation: Aquinas distinguishes self-evidence in itself from self-evidence to us. Predicate-in-the-account-of-the-subject gives the first; someone ignorant of the subject’s definition need not recognize it. This is the definition used in the natural-law context, not a claim that a corpus premise has already earned a self_evident marking.
